Header: Groundnut Rosette Virus Kadukutu, Khate in Chichewa; Kaligwiti in Tumbuka

Prevention: Early planting with the first good rains

Plant at correct plant spacing to reduce disease spread i.e. 75cm between ridges and 15cm between plant stations for long duration varieties; 60cm between ridges and 10cm between plant stations for short duration varieties
Crop rotation with maize or other cereals to avoid carry over of the disease between seasons
Intercropping with cereals hampers the spread of the aphid vector
Remove and destroy volunteer groundnut plants from the field because they may become source of inoculum in the next season
Keep the field weed free to prevent aphids which transmit rosette virus
Monitoring: This disease is vectored by aphids.
Examine for presence of aphid vectors (especially on young shoots).
Monitor plants weekly for both the disease symptoms and presence of aphids
The disease appears in two forms - yellow and green
Look for yellow twisted and distorted leaves for yellow rosette, while green mosaic is manifested by mottling of younger leaves while older leaves are dark green and reduced in size
Both forms of rosette lead to stunting and inability to produce pods
Start control methods as soon as disease symptoms are seen
When aphids are seen commence control if economically viable (see yellow control measures)
Direct Control: Rogue out and destroy infected plants either by burning or burying
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
There are no chemicals available to manage this disease but insecticides can be used to manage the aphids which transmit the virus
Applied when aphids appear, one or two additional applications could made based on scouting.
Allow 21 days between application and harvest.
Hazardous, the chemical should be applied when aphids appear and repeated as necessary.
Allow 14 days between application and harvest.
